You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — surviving registrant (Spirit Realty Capital, Inc.) realized record, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The surviving corporation continued as a public
> NYSE registrant under the same CIK (1308606) and IRS Employer Identification Number
> (20-1676382), renamed Spirit Realty Capital, Inc.; its realized record is traced through
> its subsequent annual report. The outcome window is fixed at the fiscal year 2016 annual
> report (filed February 24, 2017), roughly 3.5 years after closing. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting continuity within the outcome window
- The surviving registrant continued to file with the SEC as Spirit Realty Capital, Inc.,
  a NYSE-listed company trading under the symbol "SRC," and filed a Form 10-K for the
  fiscal year ended December 31, 2016. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The FY2016 annual report describes the registrant as "a self-administered and
  self-managed REIT with in-house capabilities, including acquisition, portfolio
  management, asset management, credit research, real estate research, legal, finance and
  accounting and capital markets." [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Best-documented realized financial record
- Net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders was $97,446 thousand for fiscal
  year 2016; the five-year selected financial data reports net income (loss) of 97,446 /
  93,212 / (36,945) / (1,616) / (76,233) thousand for 2016, 2015, 2014, 2013 and 2012
  respectively (positive in 2015-2016 following net losses in 2012-2014). [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Impairment charges were $88,275 thousand for 2016 (five-year series: 88,275 / 70,695 /
  37,598 / (185) / 8,918 thousand for 2016 through 2012). [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Goodwill on the balance sheet was $254,340 thousand at December 31, 2016, down from
  $264,350 thousand at December 31, 2015; total assets were $7,677,971 thousand. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Realized portfolio scale
- As of December 31, 2016 the registrant's undepreciated gross investment in real estate
  and loans totaled approximately $8.2 billion, representing 2,615 properties (2,541 owned
  outright); owned properties were approximately 98.2% occupied with a weighted average
  remaining lease term of approximately 10.7 years. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- During 2016 the registrant purchased 269 properties for an aggregate gross investment of
  $704.9 million. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Documented organizational disruption over the window
- During the quarter ended December 31, 2015 the registrant "made the strategic decision to
  relocate the Company's headquarters from Scottsdale, Arizona to Dallas, Texas," incurring
  $7.1 million of restructuring charges in 2015, the majority of which were estimated
  employee separation costs. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Compensation expense in 2015 reflected acceleration of approximately $2.2 million of cash
  and non-cash stock compensation "related to the departure of certain executive officers
  during the year ended December 31, 2015." [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Documented internal-control / accounting disruption over the window
- In October 2016 the registrant identified a deficiency in its internal control over
  financial reporting considered a material weakness, "which... led to the restatement of
  our audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2015 and
  our interim unaudited consolidated financial statements for the quarters ended March 31,
  2015, June 30, 2015, September 30, 2015, March 31, 2016 and June 30, 2016." [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The material weakness related to "our failure to maintain effective procedures and
  controls over the evaluation of and accounting for goodwill related to the disposal of
  assets and the allocation of goodwill to held for sale assets in determining impairment
  charges"; the registrant stated it had remediated the material weakness as of December
  31, 2016. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Tenant concentration and market data
- The registrant's largest tenant exposure was Shopko (leases guaranteed by Specialty
  Retail Shops Holding Corp.), whose revenues "represented 8.2% of our Normalized Rental
  Revenue for the month ended December 31, 2016." [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The closing sale price of the common stock on February 21, 2017 was $10.84, with
  approximately 2,827 stockholders of record. [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Within the fixed outcome window the surviving public registrant operated at expanded
  scale (2,615 properties, ~$8.2 billion gross investment, 98.2% occupied) and reported
  positive net income attributable to common stockholders in 2015-2016 ($97.4 million in
  2016) after net losses in 2012-2014; over the same period it recorded documented
  organizational disruption (a 2015 headquarters relocation with $7.1 million of
  restructuring/employee-separation charges and departures of certain executive officers)
  and a documented internal-control material weakness over goodwill accounting that forced
  restatement of its 2015 and interim 2015-2016 financial statements before being remediated
  by year-end 2016, alongside single-tenant concentration (Shopko, 8.2% of normalized rental
  revenue). [SRC: SEC accession 0001308606-17-000012, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

[SLICE END]
